articles.title: Trump Media group stares down $1bn debt crunch as bitcoin bet fades
articles.summary: The Trump family's media group may soon be forced to sell hundreds of millions' worth of assets, including some of its crypto holdings, or take...
articles.body:
The Trump family's media group may soon be forced to sell hundreds of millions' worth of assets, including some of its crypto holdings, or take on costly new borrowing as it comes under pressure to repay up to $1bn in debt.

Trump Media & Technology Group (TMTG), which runs the Truth Social app and is controlled by Donald Trump's family, faces a November 30 deadline to repay convertible bonds it sold last May to fund its creation of a "bitcoin treasury" to hoard digital currency.

But shares in TMTG have plunged and bitcoin has fallen by about a third in the past year, despite the Trump administration ushering in a more permissive era for cryptocurrencies.

The company's waning share price, which is down more than 60 per cent this year to $4.64, has meant lenders to the company who had hoped to convert their notes to stock at $34.72 are deeply out of the money.

Noteholders have therefore been left with little incentive to hold the bonds rather than forcing the company to repay them for cash at face value at the end of the month.

The Trump family media group has placed crypto at the heart of its business, with its former chief executive and chair Devin Nunes calling it a "crucial part of our assets".

Despite President Trump previously calling bitcoin a "scam" in 2021, he has become an ardent supporter of the asset in his second term and pledged to make the US the "crypto capital of the world".

A potential debt redemption of $1bn would further strain the lossmaking media group's finances and could force it to part with some of its cryptocurrency investments, the company's most valuable asset worth around $1.36bn at the end of the third quarter.

TMTG reported a loss of $234mn for the nine months to September.

One investor who is demanding repayment said he expected others would do the same. "Everyone will," he said. "It makes no sense not to."

The looming debt repayment comes at a pivotal moment for the company — whose largest shareholder is President Trump — as it seeks to close a merger with lossmaking nuclear fusion start-up TAE Technologies by the end of the year. TMTG has already lent TAE $300mn.

Although TMTG's interim CEO Kevin McGurn has boasted of its "big balance sheet", many of the company's almost $2.5bn in assets may not be immediately available to generate cash to pay bondholders.

In its most recent quarterly filing, TMTG said it could enter a credit facility to refinance all or a portion of the convertible notes. But it also said such a move could be on unfavourable terms at a high interest rate and may not happen.
authors: George Steer and Antoine Gara and Ramsay Hodgson

articles.title: Hyperliquid's HYPE Token Shows Resilience as Crypto Market Crash Deepens
articles.summary: Hyperliquid's HYPE is outperforming Bitcoin and Ethereum amid the crypto crash. Bitunix analysts explain what's next.
articles.body:
Hyperliquid's HYPE token has lost roughly a quarter of its value since its peak. Yet amid the latest crypto market crash, it is holding up better than Bitcoin and Ethereum. Its derivatives market offers one possible explanation.

HYPE traded near $73 on Friday, down approximately 7% over seven days. Bitcoin lost more than 9% during the same period, while Ethereum dropped nearly 14%.

The token's recent decline followed a rally above $95 in late October, driven partly by excitement over a partnership involving Trade.xyz and Intercontinental Exchange, the New York Stock Exchange's parent company.

Why HYPE Is Holding Up Better Than Bitcoin and Ethereum

According to Bitunix's latest research, HYPE's notional open interest on Hyperliquid declined from $1.21 billion to $1.07 billion, approximately 12%.

Ethereum's open interest on the same platform fell more than 52% over a comparable period.

Open interest measures the value of outstanding futures positions. A smaller decline suggests traders have maintained more exposure to HYPE despite falling prices, although price changes also affect the dollar value of positions.

Bitunix also identified an early HYPE whale holding over $40 million in unrealized profits as of November 12.

Meanwhile, Hyperliquid Strategies reported holding 38.52 million HYPE, approximately 16% of circulating supply, as of September 30.

Why the Broader Crypto Market Keeps Falling

Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 on Friday, reaching approximately $68,700. Ethereum slipped toward $1,930.

Institutional withdrawals remain a concern. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded another $284.1 million in outflows on November 12, their sixth consecutive negative session.

Data shows approximately $2.8 billion in withdrawals since October 30.

Ethereum ETFs also lost $70.5 million on November 12.

Persistent US inflation has strengthened expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. Falling prices have also triggered leveraged liquidations, accelerating the downturn.

WhaleRadar data showed $641 million in HYPE shorts against $515 million in longs among tracked large traders on November 13.

$70 remains the immediate level to watch.

Below that, the 200-day moving average near $68.60 offers another potential support area.

A deeper decline could threaten leveraged long positions clustered around $65.50.

A recovery above $74.40, followed by 76–77, would improve the short-term outlook.

HYPE's relative strength is encouraging, but sustained price recovery will depend on fresh buying demand and whether existing support levels survive the broader market downturn.

articles.title: Bitcoin's four-year cycle is about to turn bullish — if history repeats: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Bitcoin’s slide has hit the window where past bear markets bottomed.
articles.body:
Bitcoin just lost about a sixth of its value in four days, sliding to its lowest level since July. If its four-year cycle holds, the selling is running short on time.

From Wednesday afternoon to its low Saturday night near $62,000, bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) fell about 17%, erasing roughly $250 billion in market value, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. At that low it was down about half from its record. It also slipped below its 200-day moving average , a long-term trend line traders watch closely.

Scott Melker, host of The Daily Wolf, used to think the cycle was dead.

"I was actually a deep believer that the four-year cycle was over," Melker told Yahoo Finance at its Invest conference Thursday.

But bitcoin "topped almost to the day of when any four-year cycle predictor would have [pointed to]," he said, and the yearlong slide since then "really does align."

The clock is based on the halving , which cuts the reward for mining new bitcoin in half about every four years and slows the coin's supply growth. The last four came in 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024, all presidential election years. Each cycle's record followed 12 to 18 months later.

The peaks have arrived on a near-identical schedule. Bitcoin's October 2025 record came 1,426 days after its November 2021 peak, according to Yahoo Finance calculations using CoinMarketCap data. The two peaks before that were 1,424 days apart.

The last three bear markets bottomed 12 to 13 months after the peak, the same pattern that showed up when the Binance hack knocked $100 billion off crypto . Bitcoin just passed 13 months since its Oct. 6, 2025 record.

This cycle has already gone off script once.

Bitcoin's lowest price so far came July 1, near $57,750. That was just nine months after the peak, and 54% below the record. Past bear markets cut far deeper, by 77% to 85%. If July was the bottom, this was the shortest and shallowest bitcoin bear market yet.

That leaves two paths. Bitcoin could revisit the early July low, about 7% below Saturday's low, and turn from there. Or July was the bottom, and the latest slide ends at a higher low. Either way, if the cycle holds, the calendar points to a turn in the coming weeks or months.

The midterm elections line up too. Each of the last three bear-market lows came within about 10 weeks after a midterm vote, and this year's was early November. In the year after each of those lows, bitcoin more than doubled.

Still, three cycles is a small sample, and the pattern has broken before. In March 2024, bitcoin set a record ahead of that year's halving, a first.

articles.title: Interest in Trump’s meme coin dinner fades as $TRUMP sinks to record lows
articles.summary: By Michelle Conlin and Tom Bergin NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinn...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Nov 16 (Reuters) - As winners were being determined on Monday for President Donald Trump's third crypto gala dinner, scheduled for November 22 at his golf club outside Washington, the president's meme coin was trading near 92 cents, a bruising tumble from its high ‌in 2025 of more than $74.

At the peak of Trump's popularity, the token's price surged more than 60% when the first contest was announced in April 2025. Wealthy ‌crypto investors collectively wagered $148 million on what the president promoted as the "most EXCLUSIVE INVITATION in the world." The holdings needed to win a seat at the dinner ranged from $59,000 to $18.5 million.

Today, interest in the third meme coin dinner ​contest has collapsed. It invited 185 holders of the token, known as $TRUMP, to register and see who held the largest amounts during the contest scoring period from September 30 to November 16. The leaderboard at closing showed only 130 crypto wallets — holding a combined $8.6 million — a 94% drop from the first dinner.

The top 29 wallets will be awarded a "Special VIP Reception" with "YOUR FAVORITE PRESIDENT," according to the contest's website, along with VIP seating at the dinner.

This will be the third time Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands, has qualified for the dinner, but the first where ‌he will be at the VIP reception with the president. He ⁠came in at 26th on the leaderboard with about $41,000 in time-weighted Trump token holdings.

"You can be in a room with the president of the United States, arguably one of the most powerful people in the world," said Christensen. "So why would I not go if it cost me ⁠almost nothing to go?"

His 23-year-old sister, Gabrielle Felen, is also coming along. She bought about 2,000 Trump tokens. She was disappointed she did not make the top 120 — now, she will not get the gift bag.

The contest's muted results come at a time when the Trump family's other crypto-connected equities and ventures have also deflated to record lows. Together, outside investors in ​the ​five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5 billion, according to Reuters estimates.

Most of those losses ​came before the midterm elections in which the Democrats dealt a heavy ‌defeat to Trump's Republican Party, a result that sent prices even lower.

Because the price of the Trump token has continued to fall sharply during the holding period in the run-up to the dinner, the winners have lost millions of dollars in recent weeks.
authors: By Michelle Conlin and Tom Bergin

articles.title: JPMorgan is working on AI agent transactions, and wants to keep humans out of it to make sure ...
articles.summary: America’s biggest bank JPMorgan Chase is exploring a future where artificial intelligence agents will be able to negotiate, agree on terms and also
articles.body: America’s biggest bank JPMorgan Chase is exploring a future where artificial intelligence agents will be able to negotiate, agree on terms and also execute payments with one another without direct human intervention, but the banking giant said that strict controls will be required to make sure that the technology tays within predefined limits. According to a report by CNBC, JPMorgan’s blockchain unit Kinexys and South Korea's Hyundai Card have already completed an initial proof-of-concept which tested how AI agents could handle financial transactions autonomously. The pilot also involved a simulated foreign-exchange transaction designed to help Hyundai Card maintain Euro liquidity in its blockchain-based deposit account.AI agents negotiating with each other is the next goal: JPMorganThe report further states that the next phase of the project will focus on testing what happens when multiple AI agents interact directly with a financial ecosystem, instead of simply carrying out predefined instructions. "What happens when agents are negotiating, agreeing directly with each other and then making payments? What does that actually look like?" said Wee Kee Toh, Global Head of Kinexys Insights at JPMorgan. Speaking to CNBC, Toh said the companies are targeting the first half of 2027 for a more advanced phase that explores autonomous agent-to-agent interactions. "That, I would say, is really the biggest part of what we want to get as an expansion of the phase one scope," he said.JPMorgan wants transactions to remain within strict guardrailsWhile the AI agents could eventually handle complex financial operations independently, JPMorgan feels that governance and oversight still remain the biggest challenge. As per Toh, developing the technology itself was not particularly difficult. The greater hurdle was figuring out accountability and managing the risks associated with allowing AI systems to move money without direct human supervision. In order to address these concerns, Kinexys has built a framework that confines AI agents to authorised parameters and automatically rejects transactions that exceed their permissions."You are going to draw a box around the agent. The agent will never be able to do anything out of the box," Toh said. For example, an AI agent authorised to execute transactions worth up to $5 million would be unable to complete any payment above that threshold.The approach is designed to keep humans out of the transaction process while ensuring agents cannot act beyond predetermined rules and controls.First blockchain-based autonomous treasury testTaking about the initial trials, JPMorgan described it as the first private blockchain-based autonomous bank-agent-to-client-agent test for corporate treasury management. The proof-of-concept included a Hyundai Card AI agent starting a foreign-exchange transaction over Kinexys' blockchain infrastructure without direct involvement. JPMorgan has still not announced a commercial deployment of the technology despite successfully completing the pilot.Partnership could expand across Hyundai groupAlong with this, the companies are also working on evaluating, if the collaboration could be extended to other businesses within Hyundai Motor Group. According to Toh, Hyundai Card's links to the wider group were one of the factors that made the company an attractive partner for the project. Hyundai Motor Group currently owns a majority stake in Hyundai Card through Hyundai Motor, Kia and Hyundai Commercial.Growing push into blockchain paymentsThe AI-agent initiative comes as both companies continue investing in blockchain-based financial infrastructure. Earlier this year, Hyundai Card said it completed a proof-of-concept involving a $20,000 USDT stablecoin transfer between Hyundai Motor's US and Mexican subsidiaries, with settlement and verification taking an average of seven minutes.Meanwhile, Kinexys said in August that it had processed more than $4 trillion in transactions since inception, averaging about $7 billion in daily transaction volume. JPMorgan has also been expanding its digital asset offerings, including the rollout of its dollar-denominated deposit token JPMD for institutional clients.For JPMorgan, the long-term vision is not simply using AI to automate payments, but enabling autonomous agents to negotiate and settle transactions with one another while operating inside tightly controlled boundaries designed to prevent unauthorised actions.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? Find out in the TOI AI Masterclass.
